# Results — Study 428 (Stochastic RSI) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — StochRSI(14,14,3,3)
on daily closes turned into a stateful **long-flat** timing rule (long on %K crossing up
through 20, flat on %K crossing down through 80), entered with **one day of execution lag**,
charged **1 bp one-way × NAV traded**, measured **excess of cash** so the part-time-in-cash
rule is raced apples-to-apples. Headline tape: **SPY**, with a 5-ETF panel cross-check.
As-of **2026-06-23** (the last complete daily bar; the in-progress 2026-06-24 bar is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window (full pull) | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| SPY | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-23 | `dae9c2290246` |
| QQQ | 1999-03-10 → 2026-06-23 | `505b4bf968c0` |
| IWM | 2000-05-26 → 2026-06-23 | `602c93f8034f` |
| DIA | 1998-01-20 → 2026-06-23 | `105c73f0fc7a` |
| EFA | 2001-08-27 → 2026-06-23 | `45652b86a02b` |

Bars are Yahoo! auto-adjusted (total-return) daily OHLCV. The headline SPY race runs on the
common 1993-11-12 → 2026-06-23 index (n = **8,206** trading days) after the SMA(200) /
StochRSI warm-up shared by all legs.

## The headline race — SPY long-flat, net 1bp, excess of cash

| Strategy | net Sharpe | HAC *t* | ann. excess | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **StochRSI long-flat** | **0.31** | **+2.03** | +4.44% | −57.5% |
| Plain RSI(14) 30/70 | 0.34 | +2.31 | +5.08% | −55.2% |
| SMA(50/200) trend | 0.75 | +4.99 | +10.40% | −33.7% |
| **Buy & hold SPY** | **0.64** | +4.26 | +12.03% | −55.2% |

- StochRSI's net Sharpe **clears the HAC *t* = 2 bar** (gross *t* = +2.10, net *t* = +2.03)
  — **but that is necessary, not sufficient.** A *t* ≥ 2 here certifies only that the mean
  return is non-zero, which an up-drifting index hands to *any* part-time-long rule for free.
- Buy-and-hold (Sharpe **0.64**) and even the much simpler SMA(50/200) filter (**0.75**)
  both beat it. The "extra sensitivity" of the double oscillator costs return, not adds it.

## Strip the beta — the timing alpha is negative

Regressing the StochRSI net return on the market excess return:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| β (market loading) | 0.58 |
| Timing alpha (intercept) | **−2.66%/yr** |
| Alpha *t* | **−1.67** |

The rule is on average ~58% invested; every dollar of its return is borrowed equity beta,
and the timing *subtracts* value. This is the canonical trap the inference bar guards against.

## The same-exposure coin — no timing skill

Holding **time-in-market fixed** (55.1% of days) and randomising *which* days, over 50 seeds:

| | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|
| StochRSI actual timing | 0.30 |
| Random-timing coin (mean) | 0.41 |
| Random-timing coin (95% band) | [0.18, 0.63] |

**84%** of random in/out schedules with the same exposure *beat* StochRSI. The rule times
worse than chance.

## Benchmark Sharpe-gap races (block bootstrap, StochRSI − benchmark)

| Race | ΔSharpe | 95% CI | P(StochRSI not better) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| vs buy-and-hold | **−0.33** | [−0.53, −0.13] | 99.9% |
| vs plain RSI(14) | **−0.03** | [−0.33, +0.24] | 59.7% |
| vs SMA(50/200) | −0.44 | [−0.77, −0.12] | 99.8% |

The gap vs plain RSI straddles zero — **stacking the stochastic on RSI is a statistical tie**.
The sign-flip permutation *p* on the net series is 0.037, but that only rejects a *zero* mean
(the equity drift again); it says nothing about timing skill.

## Long-short variant (net 1bp)

Shorting the "overbought" signal instead of going flat makes it strictly worse:

| | net Sharpe | HAC *t* | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| StochRSI long-short | −0.18 | −1.15 | −86.7% |

The overbought exits land inside ongoing uptrends, so the short leg bleeds.

## Cost sweep & turnover (SPY long-flat)

Turnover is ~**15.4 round-trips/yr**, so costs are *not* the binding constraint — the rule
trails buy-and-hold even gross:

| round-trip cost | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|
| 0 bp (gross) | 0.31 |
| 1 bp | 0.30 |
| 2 bp | 0.29 |
| 5 bp | 0.26 |

No cost level lets it catch the 0.64 buy-and-hold line.

## Panel cross-check (long-flat, net 1bp)

| Ticker | StochRSI net Sharpe | buy-and-hold Sharpe | ΔSharpe vs plain RSI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 0.31 | 0.64 | −0.03 |
| QQQ | 0.20 | 0.45 | +0.07 |
| IWM | 0.18 | 0.48 | −0.12 |
| DIA | 0.27 | 0.56 | −0.08 |
| EFA | 0.41 | 0.43 | +0.28 |

Every ETF's StochRSI rule loses to its own buy-and-hold, and the vs-RSI gap has no consistent
sign — SPY is not a fluke.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to time

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`), the StochRSI edge **over a
same-exposure coin** rises sharply when the tape *trends* and turns negative when it whipsaws:

| Planted AR(1) `mean_rev` | StochRSI Sharpe | coin Sharpe | edge |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| −0.20 (trending) | +0.91 | +0.42 | **+0.48** |
| −0.10 (trending) | +0.70 | +0.36 | +0.34 |
| 0.00 (martingale) | +0.45 | +0.34 | +0.11 |
| +0.10 (mild whipsaw) | +0.35 | +0.34 | +0.01 |
| +0.25 (whipsaw) | +0.19 | +0.37 | −0.18 |
| +0.40 (whipsaw) | +0.10 | +0.31 | −0.21 |

The harness *can* bank a timing edge when one is planted — so the real-tape null is a
statement about SPY's short-horizon dynamics, not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The net HAC *t* = +2.03 is harvested equity beta (β = 0.58); the timing
  alpha is **−2.66%/yr** (*t* = −1.67, wrong sign), and a same-exposure coin beats the rule
  **84%** of the time. No timing skill.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net Sharpe 0.31 vs buy-and-hold 0.64; the gap is negative in
  99.9% of block bootstraps and no cost level closes it. You pay costs to underperform doing
  nothing.
- **Adds over RSI? — NOT SUPPORTED.** ΔSharpe vs plain RSI = −0.03, 95% CI [−0.33, +0.24] —
  the second oscillator is statistically indistinguishable from plain RSI.
